## [summary] Cloud now carries the quarter, and its buildout needs outside capital

Cloud now carries the quarter, and its buildout needs outside capital

The operating business improved faster than the 26% fall in earnings per share suggests. Revenue of $127.6 billion rose 24.7% , operating margin reached 31.8% , and Google Cloud revenue rose to $30.7 billion from $15.2 billion a year earlier, at a 36.2% segment margin. The reported decline came from the portfolio, not the business: other income swung to a $8.2 billion expense from $12.8 billion of income a year earlier, largely net unrealized losses on marketable equity securities, mainly SpaceX, and lower net unrealized gains on non-marketable equity securities. Other income (expense), net 

What changed for a holder is the funding model. Nine-month capital expenditure more than doubled to $132.0 billion from $63.6 billion and exceeded operating cash flow of $127.1 billion , leaving free cash flow of -$4.8 billion , and the gap was funded with senior notes, a June equity offering, mandatory convertible preferred and at-the-market sales. Debt Common stock Preferred stock Equity sales 

Our judgment is to keep the position but read it as a capital-reinvestment story rather than a cash-return story. That rests on Cloud's incremental revenue keeping a segment margin near the reported level, on TPU hardware staying a minority of Cloud's increase, and on assets now under construction earning more than the debt and equity raised to fund them. The transmission is arithmetic: every 100 basis points of Cloud segment margin is worth about $1.23 billion of annualized segment operating income (not revenue) at the third-quarter revenue run-rate, or about $307 million a quarter; $298 million of preferred dividends and $967 million of quarterly interest expense sit between operating income and per-share earnings. Where the filing stops short of a number, the effect stays a sensitivity rather than a figure we can carry into a valuation.

_(Bindings: 21, Sources: 21, Charts: none)_

## [highlights] Cloud margin and Search growth lifted operating margin to 31.8%

Cloud margin and Search growth lifted operating margin to 31.8%

Google Cloud earned $11.1 billion of operating income on $30.7 billion of revenue, a 36.2% margin against 23.7% a year earlier, and the segment's operating income rose $7.5 billion. The 10-Q attributes the increase to higher revenue, partly offset by inventory and related costs for TPU system sales and by technical infrastructure usage costs. Google Cloud segment profitability Cloud is now 24.1% of consolidated revenue versus 14.8% a year earlier, so the segment's margin now moves the group margin.

Google Services grew revenue 10.6% to $96.3 billion and lifted its margin to 40.7% from 38.5% , helped by a lower legal charge and despite higher traffic acquisition costs. Legal settlements Search & other, still the largest line at $63.4 billion , grew 12.0% in the quarter and 15.8% over nine months; the traffic acquisition cost rate slipped to 20.0% from 20.1%. Contracted demand backs the growth: remaining performance obligations were $567.7 billion , of which $560.8 billion sits in Google Cloud. Total backlog equals 1.11x annualised third-quarter revenue, though that ratio is not comparable with prior periods: the 10-Q discloses that in the first quarter of 2026 the company elected to also include contracts with an original expected term of one year or less. Revenue Backlog Google Cloud revenue Operating cash flow rose 13.2% to $127.1 billion over nine months even though a $5.2 billion European Commission fine and interest left the bank in July.

## [versus-prior] No dated guidance was delivered, so only qualitative forward statements can be scored

No dated guidance was delivered, so only qualitative forward statements can be scored

The frozen expectations bundle attached to this filing contains no dated management guidance, no previously published watch condition, no model driver and no verified industry mapping, so those items are not measurable rather than met or missed. The only forward statements available are the company's own, inside the 10-Q, and two can be scored. Management said it expects to significantly increase 2026 investment in technical infrastructure relative to 2025; nine-month capital expenditure of $131,953 million against $63,596 million a year earlier is consistent with that, and the third quarter's $51.4 billion implies no slowdown. Management also repeated that existing cash and cash flows will fund commitments for at least the next twelve months; with free cash flow of -$4.8 billion over nine months, that statement now depends on continued access to debt and equity markets, used in June for an equity offering, a private placement and mandatory convertible preferred, and for senior notes issued during the nine months. Common stock Preferred stock Debt Capital expenditures Liquidity and capital resources 

Three evidence limits shape the comparison. No earnings call transcript is on file for this quarter, so management's reasoning cannot be tested against its own words beyond the 10-Q and the earnings release. The comparison tooling returned no earlier prepared filing for the commitments and liquidity sections, so wording changes against the prior 10-Q could not be diffed; prior-year figures here come from this filing's own comparative columns. The frozen public-research library holds no reports, with both macro and industry coverage marked uncovered, so no industry claim is adopted and no industry question is interpreted.

One judgment needs revising. Reading Cloud as a consumption business whose margin expansion is a durable run-rate is no longer safe: the segment's revenue now mixes platform consumption with TPU product sales, and the majority of the TPU agreements' revenue is scheduled for 2027. Google Cloud revenue The 36.2% margin should be read as a blended outcome for a quarter in which, on our reading, hardware sales contributed to revenue growth while, per the filing, inventory costs for TPU systems partly offset that increase in segment operating income. Google Cloud segment profitability Our revised assumption is a lower through-cycle Cloud margin than this quarter prints, with the direction of the mix disclosed only in 2027.

_(Bindings: 12, Sources: 12, Charts: none)_

## [overlooked] Cloud's growth includes TPU hardware that mostly lands in 2027

Cloud's growth includes TPU hardware that mostly lands in 2027

The cloud revenue discussion carries a disclosure the revenue table does not: Alphabet has signed a limited number of agreements to supply TPU systems to customers needing on-premises infrastructure, began recognising revenue from them in the second quarter of 2026, and expects the significant majority to be recognised in 2027. Google Cloud revenue The third-quarter explanation names TPU system sales as a driver of the $15.6 billion Cloud increase. Our reading is that hardware entered the quarterly comparison only in the last two quarters, but the filing does not quantify its share, so it may or may not be material; if it is, the 102.6% Cloud growth is partly a product-sale event with a gross margin the filing does not disclose, and revenue recognition pulls toward 2027. Every 100 basis points of Cloud segment margin is worth about $1.23 billion of annualized segment operating income (not revenue) at the third-quarter revenue run-rate, so the mix question is worth more than a footnote.

Cloud's growth also includes an acquisition the segment comparison cannot separate. The $29.5 billion Wiz acquisition closed on 11 March 2026 and its results are included in Google Cloud for the whole third quarter, while the year-earlier quarter contained none of it; the filing does not quantify Wiz's revenue contribution, and the filing does not disclose how much of the 102.6% segment growth was acquired rather than organic. Wiz acquisition Acquisitions and divestitures 

Cash leaves before earnings arrive in two places. The 2018 Android decision was upheld on appeal on 2 July 2026, and the $5.2 billion fine and interest, already accrued, was paid in July, inside this quarter, so the earnings charge fell in an earlier period while the cash left operating cash flow in 2026. Separately, short-term accrued legal and regulatory fines and settlements were still $13.8 billion at 30 September 2026.

The preferred stock adds a per-share cost that the operating narrative hides. The 19 million 6.25% mandatory convertible preferred shares issued in June for $19.0 billion net took $298 million out of earnings available to common holders in the quarter, of which $234 million was cash paid and the rest accrual; the gap between the $26,468 million net income and the $26,170 million available to common is exactly that charge. Preferred and common dividends Dilution is already visible: basic weighted-average shares rose to 12,256 million from 12,086 million , up 1.4% , and $27.6 billion remains available under the at-the-market program.

Other Bets is now partly financed on its own. Waymo signed a $5.0 billion senior secured term loan in October 2026 maturing in 2032 at Term SOFR plus 5.25%, secured by Waymo assets and expressly not guaranteed by Alphabet, so the borrowing now sits with Waymo's own creditors. The segment's quarterly operating loss widened to $2,047 million from $1,426 million .

_(Bindings: 18, Sources: 17, Charts: none)_

## [risks] A $21 billion decline in other income (expense), net accompanied a 26.1% EPS decline while operating income improved

A $21 billion decline in other income (expense), net accompanied a 26.1% EPS decline while operating income improved

The per-share decline is an investment mark, not an operating one. Third-quarter other income (expense), net moved from $12,759 million of income to $(8,221) million of expense, as net losses on equity securities of $(8,664) million replaced prior-year gains of $10,734 million . Net income available to common fell to $26,170 million from $34,979 million and diluted EPS to $2.12 from $2.87 , a 26.1% decline, while operating income rose to $40,576 million from $31,228 million . Other income (expense), net The filing discloses no counterfactual EPS effect, and the swing is pre-tax and largely reverses with the market prices of the stakes held, so this is the one part of the quarter that says little about the business.

Costs below the operating line are now real and recurring. Interest expense reached $967 million in the quarter, and the preferred shares, first issued in June 2026, declared and accrued $298 million of dividends, of which $234 million was paid in cash and the rest accrued. Both sit between operating income and earnings per share, and the dividend has no year-earlier counterpart, so the per-share translation of operating growth is now weaker than the segment margins imply. Mandatory convertible preferred 

Cloud's 36.2% margin may not be a run-rate. Segment operating margin rose to 36.2% from 23.7% on revenue that doubled, and the filing says the significant majority of revenues from the limited number of TPU supply agreements will be recognized in 2027, with Cloud revenue already including TPU product sales. We assume the hardware portion carries a lower gross margin than the consumption business, which would pull the through-cycle margin below today's level; the filing does not disclose TPU revenue or its margin, so the size of the dilution is unknown. TPU supply agreements 

Capital spending now exceeds internal cash generation. Nine-month operating cash flow of $127,149 million fell short of $131,953 million of capital expenditure, leaving free cash flow of $(4,804) million , and $145,270 million of property and equipment is not yet in service and will begin depreciating as it is placed into use. Against that, material purchase commitments total $924.4 billion, of which $802.1 billion relates to multi-year commitments for technical infrastructure and inventory, energy take-or-pay contracts and content licenses and $213.4 billion of that total is due within twelve months. Leases signed but not yet commenced add $130.5 billion . Purchase commitments 

The cushion is smaller than the headline cash balance. Cash, equivalents and short-term marketable securities were $265.1 billion , of which $75.2 billion is SpaceX shares subject to short-term restrictions on the ability to sell, so the immediately available cushion is smaller than that total. Beyond the contractual amounts, the filing discloses $75.7 billion of backstop obligations relating to data centers, including data center lease payments and associated energy costs: $48.0 billion is executed with third-party data center providers and accounted for as credit derivatives, and $27.7 billion represents obligations to put future backstops in place, $10.0 billion of it with Crux AI, a related party. Separate financial guarantees totaled $22.8 billion , primarily to support counterparty procurement of long-lead-time equipment for future power purchase and energy agreements, and, separately, $6.6 billion of potential repurchases of previously sold TPU hardware and embedded software. Commitments and contingencies These are contingent exposures rather than payments due on a schedule, but they grow with the infrastructure build and are not netted against the reported cash.

Legal and segment drags persist. Accrued legal and regulatory obligations of $13.8 billion remain on the balance sheet after $5.2 billion of fine and interest was paid in July 2026 following the European Court of Justice's dismissal of the appeal, and Other Bets widened its operating loss to $(2,047) million from $(1,426) million . ## [what-to-watch] Four disclosures decide whether the current margin and funding path hold

Four disclosures decide whether the current margin and funding path hold

Cloud product-sale mix and the 2027 recognition schedule

Watch whether the fourth-quarter 10-Q or the 2026 annual report quantifies TPU system sales inside Cloud revenue and whether segment margin holds near 36%. A large hardware share with a lower margin would confirm the revised, lower through-cycle assumption; a stable margin with no hardware emphasis would weaken it.

Depreciation as assets enter service

$145.3 billion of property and equipment, 29.9% of gross property and equipment, was not yet in service at 30 September 2026. If all of it were placed in service at once and depreciated straight-line over five years, annual depreciation would be about $29.1 billion at full run-rate; assets entering service over several years would phase that in. For scale, the $21,955 million charged in the first nine months of 2026 runs at roughly $29.3 billion annualized. The first evidence is the depreciation line and the not-yet-in-service balance in the next 10-Q.

Capital expenditure against operating cash flow, and the 12-month commitment wall

Full-year capital expenditure, full-year free cash flow and any draw on the $213.4 billion of commitments due within twelve months. A second nine-month period of capex above operating cash flow with no buyback resumption would keep the equity-issuance channel open; a return to operating cash flow above capital expenditure, meaning positive free cash flow, plus any buyback restart would show the funding shift was temporary.

Share count, preferred conversion and the at-the-market balance

Weighted-average shares rose 1.4% year over year with $27.6 billion left on the at-the-market program, and the conversion terms of the mandatory convertible preferred are set out in the preferred stock note. Per-share earnings need the conversion ratio and date to be modelled; the next 10-Q's diluted share count is the check.

Portfolio marks and the tax rate

The first nine months' earnings included a $126.8 billion net gain on debt and equity securities, and the third-quarter effective tax rate was 18.2%. Quarterly moves in those marks change reported earnings without changing operating profit, and a higher tax rate would reduce reported net earnings.

附注与表外风险挖掘极深：完整挖出 $924.4B 采购承诺（12 个月内 $213.4B）、$130.5B 未起租租赁、$265.1B 现金证券中含 $75.2B 受限 SpaceX 股票、$75.7B 数据中心兜底（含 $10.0B 关联方 Crux AI）、Waymo $5.0B 无追索权定期贷款、$27.6B ATM 余额及 $13.8B 应付罚款。

negativeFeedback.suggestion: 在定期财报撰稿规范中强制要求围绕核心财务矛盾生成 1–2 张 chart_facts 趋势图（如 CapEx vs OCF/FCF、核心分部利润率演进），核心对比表必须附带 YoY % 或 bps 变动列；并禁止 risks 板块首段重复 summary 已展开的非经营损益论述。
优化 DeepSeek semantic-audit 收敛效率与附注口径约束：在撰稿 Prompt 中明确要求担保/承诺严格区分“总额与分项（of which）”、多系列可转债/优先股按系列分别表述转股率，避免 20+ 轮拉锯耗尽 140 轮预算而卡在最终发布前。
强化现金流含金量与季度斜率倒推纪律：当 FCF 转负或非经营公允价值波动巨大时，要求显式拆解递延所得税/SBC 对 OCF 的影响，补充单季环比 CapEx/OCF 趋势压力测算，并在流动性判断中先对照不受限现金余额再评估融资依赖度。
